name: Hanniel
overview: Hanniel was a male leader from the tribe of Manasseh who played a significant role in the apportioning of the Promised Land. He is specifically identified as the leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the division of the land, as recorded in Numbers 34:23. His leadership was instrumental in the distribution of territory among the tribes of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanniel means 'favored of G-d [El],' reflecting a divine favor or blessing. This proper name, mentioned in Numbers 34:23, highlights his standing and possibly the providential approval of his leadership role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Hanniel was the son of Ephod, as explicitly stated in Numbers 34:23. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hanniel's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as the appointed leader responsible for overseeing the allotment of the land to the tribe of Manasseh. This task was critical in fulfilling God's promise to the Israelites regarding their inheritance in Canaan. His leadership ensured an orderly and divinely sanctioned distribution of territory, underscoring the faithfulness of God's covenant with His people.
